newsitem.title: UK: United News drops on HTV stake purchase.
newsitem.headline: United News drops on HTV stake purchase.

text.p: Shares in United News & Media Plc dropped in pre-market trading on Friday after the company said it would take a 20 percent stake in television broadcaster HTV Plc.
United shares were down 15-1/2p at 653-1/2 by 0710 GMT while HTV shares leapt 18p to 391-1/2.

Other television stocks also gained as bid speculation revived across the industry, with Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Plc up 22-1/2p at 12.22-1/2 stg, Scottish Television Plc 6p higher at 768-1/2 and Ulster TV up 6p at 200.

News of the purchase, from Scottish TV, came just two weeks after United paid 592.5 million stg for exhibitions group Blenheim though the company said the move was an investment and it had no plans to make an offer for the whole of HTV.

Yet analysts said the move was a natural part of United's strategy under chief executive Clive Hollick, who merged his MAI group with United last year and has since sought to consolidate its media interests.
And they said it was an expected part of the restructuring of the UK media industry.
"When United bought Blenheim we were very much focusing on HTV as the next target," said Lorna Tilbian, analyst at Panmure Gordon. "They could not afford to let it fall into the Carlton camp."
Carlton Communications Plc was down 10p at 502-1/2.
Tilbian pointed out that United's advertising sales house TSMS would lose some of its clout if HTV fell into the hands of a rival television group.
And she said STV had been a likely seller of its stake since buying Caledonian newspapers.
"Once Scottish bought Caledonian it was likely they would see no synergies between Glasgow and Wales," she said, "and it was pretty inevitable Hollick would be interested to buy."
By 0823 GMT, United shares had recovered to be down just 1/2p at 668-1/2.
